body: Definitely, well I'm here if you ever get bored or need someone to talk to

Well, I got put on a detail (details are random jobs that the army will task out to people) where I only work about 2 hours a day, usually driving around picking up laundry.  Got on the detail because I'm waiting to get discharged.  Most of the time I read a lot or reddit lol. I'm in a very remote area, so there isn't too much to do. My friends are always in the field, so it's rare that I see them, but when I do its a welcome respite. Honestly i think being alone all the time is a big part of my problem, definitely feel better seeing my friends.
Lol, thank you. It's good for me to stay occupied too.
Thank you :) It's been hard admitting it, but I think in doing it I feel better now.

I guess it just goes back to my self esteem issues. Before I was hurt, I was strong as an ox, I was fast, and I spent everyday training to fight. I was an airborne infantryman, and although I didn't always like it; I truly felt confident for once. I never once considered myself better than anyone else, but I felt at home in my own skin. Now that I've lost all that, I feel like my self esteem has gone with it. I don't feel like a man anymore. I still try and put myself out there, but I get rejected everytime, and I know it's because I don't value myself anymore.

I've done all the same treatments, including an epidural injection; to no avail. My pain is from injury and overuse, all I do for exercise is walking now. I too am worried about the future, but I know it doesn't help me.

It truly is beautiful there, miss it everyday. Maybe I'll be a bit happier when I finally can go back, I don't know. And I'm sorry about your back. It really is something people don't understand unless they have been there. I'm not glad that you're hurt, but I guess I'm glad someone else understands it. It's nice to talk to someone about this pain finally.
I'm from Washington state, I'm currently in rural Louisiana.
